This publication is a systematic review/meta-analysis of existing studies, not a new patient intervention, prospective AI evaluation, or reader experiment.
This publication is a systematic review/meta-analysis of existing studies, not a new patient intervention, prospective AI evaluation, or reader experiment.
The abstract explicitly states retrospective analysis of anonymized EHRs from 30 hospitals; stratified random sampling selects records and is not patient treatment allocation.
Retrospective annual EHR cohorts and adjusted associations between remote care and later service use; no newly allocated intervention.
The authors explicitly describe a retrospective multicenter reinforcement-learning study; estimated mortality is off-policy, not outcomes from randomized AI-directed treatment.
Secondary model development on existing PAOLA-1 randomized-trial slides and outcomes. Original trial treatment assignment does not make this new histology model study a new patient RCT.
The abstract calls this retrospective proof-of-concept AI assistance and specifically requests future prospective/video validation; actual endoscopist reading comparisons are reported.
Explicitly a multicenter retrospective study of 665 patients; validation splits are not prospective new-case evaluation.
The abstract explicitly identifies a retrospective cohort of 433 subjects; classification and computational causal inference do not establish a clinical intervention trial.
The abstract explicitly states retrospective multicenter angiography model development and external testing, without allocated model-guided treatment.
Learning and policy assessment use past transplant/nutrition records from 2008–2025; prospective evaluation is future work rather than the reported design.
The authors explicitly retrospectively included lobectomy patients from 2008–2023; imaging associations are observational.
Target-trial emulation uses observational cases and propensity matching; it approximates a hypothetical trial and is not actual randomized embryo allocation.
Retrospective selection of 1,664 PET patients with angiography from a larger clinical population; three external sites provide held-out diagnostic testing, not prospective accrual.
The abstract explicitly states a multinational retrospective ocular-image study; segmentation and classifier comparisons do not establish prospective deployment.
The abstract explicitly states retrospective collection of PICC cases; internal and external image validation are not prospective patient accrual.
A reader study compares retinal specialists and AI and assesses AI-assisted clinicians on treatment-response images. Patient image-collection timing and model-freeze chronology are not given.
Thirty-six surgeons identify anatomy in 640 short video snippets with and without AI assistance. The intervention is a surgeon recognition task, not randomized patient surgery.
Junior ophthalmologists perform model-assisted ocular-GVHD diagnosis. The abstract does not establish whether the enrolled model cohorts were accrued after model completion.
The abstract explicitly reports a 120-case multireader multicase experiment with assisted junior-reader sensitivity; it does not allocate patient care.
An MRI expert reader study compares diagnostic performance on prostate cases. A virtual screening scenario is not patient-randomized screening.
Seventeen dermatologists and four models diagnose nail images. Prospective comparative study wording does not establish prospectively accrued patients or a frozen-model sequence.
Junior radiologists interpret MRI with CAD assistance, with changes in accuracy and reading time; patient care is not randomized.
Digitized cervical slides are randomized to reading sequences, with four cytopathologists crossing over after washout. Slide/reader randomization is not allocation of women to care.
Eighteen physicians predict glioma IDH status on image cohorts for comparison with two AI models; this is a reader comparison, not treatment allocation.
Radiologists assess renal tumor CT/MRI cases for comparison with MPANet. Cohort timing is not specified in the abstract.
Physicians make treatment recommendations for 300 simulated hypertension cases with model configurations. This is a human-AI decision experiment, not treatment of randomized patients.

Twelve surgical oncologists prospectively complete a randomized crossed reader experiment on 166 explicitly retrospective cases. Patient data are historical; reader sequence randomization is not a patient RCT.
Two spine surgeons predict complications with and without LLM explanations. Patient sources combine retrospective and prospective data, but model-before-accrual timing is not established.

A pre-registered three-arm randomized intervention enrolls 977 university students. It is participant randomization in a student population; the abstract does not establish selection as a patient/symptom-defined clinical cohort.

An LLM voice assistant is deployed for new patient calls in a stabilization phase followed by nurse-led real-world evaluation. Prospective use is established, but no unchanged model configuration across phases is specified.

The abstract explicitly separates retrospective development from prospectively collected internal/external cohorts. It does not state whether all validation cases arrived after model completion, so strict prospective model validation remains unresolved.

Authors report retrospective cases plus 512 prospective cases. Prior Methods audit identified unresolved conflict between the reported 2024 pilot and a model released in 2025; retain prospective collection as reported, but model-before-accrual validation is unconfirmed.

Patient queries are explicitly collected prospectively and independently scored after human/ChatGPT answers. This is answer-quality assessment, not model-guided patient treatment or a clinical reader decision experiment.

After development/validation, the LSTM undergoes prospective daily evaluation with live EHR extracts. This explicit live-prediction sequence supports prospective model validation; no patient intervention randomization is described.

A prospective study enrolls 995 adults; novices acquire ultrasound with an existing commercial real-time AI-guidance system, compared with same-session reference echocardiography. This establishes prospective use/evaluation, not patient-randomized treatment.

The model is developed on large clinical datasets and then tested in an explicitly independent prospective cohort of 1,338 children. Accrual is prospective; abstract alone does not confirm a frozen model preceded every test-case accrual.

A registered prospective test cohort is reported separately from validation, but the abstract does not specify model-lock versus accrual sequence. Regimen-specific recommendations are counterfactual model estimates, not randomized treatment assignment.

An existing commercial pathology system is evaluated prospectively in routine reporting at three NHS centers, with staged and concurrent AI-assisted workflows. This is prospective deployment evaluation without patient randomization.

A prospective observational course records 50 residents operating on porcine simulators. New experimental videos are collected, but this is surgical-skill assessment rather than a patient trial or clinical image-reader task; model timing is unspecified.

Prospective one-week routine-use evaluation collects and annotates cardiac-device recordings. PASTEC is infrastructure for future AI validation; no AI diagnostic model is validated in this reported comparison.

The review contains a newly clinic-acquired feasibility demonstration alongside reference monitors. That establishes new signal collection but does not establish frozen learned-model validation timing.

Adults with diabetes are recruited for a randomized hypothetical copay vignette. Choices and attitudes are measured, without allocating actual screening or care; this is neither patient-care RCT nor clinician reader experiment.
Exploratory prospective clinical testing and human-AI dentist comparisons are explicitly reported. The abstract does not establish model completion before prospective recruitment.

The abstract states retrospective development followed by internal, prospective, and external cohort testing. Prospective collection is reported, but strict model-before-accrual timing is not established in the abstract.

Adults undergoing endoscopy are randomized 1:1 to previously developed automated ciprofol delivery or clinician management in a prospective four-center trial. Separate development and clinical-validation groups establish actual prospective AI intervention evaluation.
Two LLMs answer 99 constructed laboratory scenarios, with expert ratings. These are simulated reasoning tests rather than newly recruited patient outcomes or clinician decisions with AI assistance.

Sixty-one volunteers prospectively wear sensor patches before and after administered vaccines, with paired serum markers. Biomarker data are newly collected, but the abstract does not establish a frozen AI model or randomized patient intervention.

Thirteen cardiac-surgery patients undergo planned sensor recordings before, during, and after hospitalization. This is prospective observational collection, not a validated AI predictor or randomized circadian intervention.

The abstract explicitly describes a prospective CLE trial while developing the Swin-based AI model. New biopsies are collected, but AI development during collection does not establish frozen-model prospective validation.

A customized model is developed and 433 patients are prospectively enrolled for shadow diagnosis comparison. The abstract does not fully establish frozen-model versus accrual timing; expert output ratings are not patient treatment allocation.

After training on earlier videos, 318 patients are prospectively randomized to real-time ENDOVISTA-ENT-assisted or conventional endoscopy. Actual patient procedure allocation establishes a clinical AI RCT.

Ultrasound videos are explicitly prospectively collected, and assisted sonographer detection is assessed. Training and validation use those collected videos, so prospective data source alone does not establish prospective locked-model validation.

Forty-eight people with chronic aphasia are randomized to actual language therapy in the model-recommended or opposite language. This is patient treatment allocation and prospective clinical testing of model-guided selection.
Psychiatrists rate generated educational vignettes. Expert content ratings are not a clinical reader decision experiment or treatment allocation; no new patient data are collected.

The abstract reports operation-time and complication comparisons but does not specify prospective recruitment, allocation, or model timing. All clinical design dimensions remain unresolved rather than inferred from favorable outcomes.

Clinical labels are assigned to simulated and existing safety-dataset messages. Message classification is not prospective patient collection, clinical intervention randomization, or a clinician decision experiment.

Retrospective report assessment is followed by a new 800-patient comprehension evaluation. Patient participation is established, but explicit prospective model timing and random allocation are not reported.

Screening/surveillance participants are recruited and randomized to EndoMind-assisted or conventional colonoscopy. This is real patient procedure allocation, not retrospective image evaluation or a reader crossover.

Report-Angel is trained on earlier image-text pairs and evaluated in author-described prospective internal/external video cohorts. Prospective collection is clear; the abstract does not fully establish locked-model versus recruitment chronology.

Age prediction is trained using existing hospital ECGs and evaluated in two independent wearable cohorts. Cohort independence alone does not establish current prospective accrual or model-before-accrual timing.
The current randomized trial assigns 261 postoperative orthopedic patients to GPT-4 WeChat support or routine doctor communication and follows actual recovery outcomes.

The analysis explicitly integrates public single-cell, spatial, and bulk transcriptomic datasets; machine learning evaluates biomarker classification rather than new clinical accrual or allocated treatment.

Four validation studies include new cognitive-test and retest assessments, but the abstract does not establish prospective frozen-AI testing or a patient-randomized care intervention. This is a digital assessment platform rather than a described learned predictor.
StructMIL is evaluated on existing Camelyon16 and PANDA benchmarks. Cross-center/scanner domain tests do not constitute prospective new patient collection or intervention.
StrokeFlow is tested on the existing public ISLES 2022 imaging benchmark, not prospectively accrued patient cases or allocated stroke care.
FlowAxis reports computational evaluations on four existing vascular benchmarks and theoretical guarantees; this is not a new clinical intervention study.
Geo-MIL experiments use three public gastric-cancer datasets, with no new prospective patient accrual or clinical intervention in the reported experiment.

Natural and intervention modules model existing refractive records and treatment cohorts. A causal-learning framework and modeled individual effects do not establish random treatment allocation in this publication.

VaTEP is an embryo-video outcome prediction framework. The abstract does not report recruitment timing, frozen-model sequence, or actual randomized embryo selection; retain unresolved clinical design labels.
KT-LLM evaluates deidentified OPTN/UNOS cohorts and policy-grounded agents, not a new randomized transplant intervention. Current prospective collection and deployment chronology are not established.
The knowledge graph reuses public biomedical links and genetic associations; drug candidates are computational predictions, not administered randomized treatments.
VertebraFormer uses a benchmark assembled from existing public/private CT datasets. Cross-domain evaluations do not establish current prospective recruitment or deployed model validation.

The abstract reports internal/external segmentation tests and surgeon workflow measurements. Acquisition timing, model-lock chronology, and patient intervention allocation are unspecified; do not infer them from time savings.
Drug-safety modeling reuses FAERS reports from 2016–2024 and computational molecular networks. Spontaneous-report analysis is not prospective collection or a randomized medication intervention.
Four language models complete irritability instruments under prompt conditions. Experimental units are model responses, not patients, clinicians, or prospectively observed clinical outcomes.
SlowFast classifies videos from 167 individuals across three splits. The abstract does not specify prospective recording or model completion before test-case accrual.

Breath samples are collected from 206 participants for fivefold cross-validation, but prospective recruitment chronology is not stated. Internal cross-validation is not prospective frozen-model validation.
CVTC is evaluated on ADNI, NACC, OASIS and other existing MRI datasets. Cross-validation and cross-dataset tests do not establish prospective patient validation.
LLM workflows are optimized and evaluated on clinical-note datasets with expert label re-adjudication. This is not an allocated patient intervention; note-source accrual timing is not specified.

Agent evaluations use oncology QA benchmarks and clinical datasets followed by physician ratings. Plan-quality ratings are not treatment allocation, and prospective patient model-testing chronology is not specified.
StyleGAN and YOLO use existing public still-image datasets. External image testing is not prospective live-colonoscopy validation or patient intervention randomization.
Gradient boosting predicts survival in four cohorts; neither random treatment allocation nor prospective model-before-accrual timing is established in the abstract.
The polygenic/lifestyle analysis uses UK Biobank and hospital genetic cohorts. Lifestyle groups are observational, so the mortality association is not a randomized intervention effect.
xHAIM is evaluated on the existing HAIM-MIMIC-MM benchmark. Multimodal prediction and generated explanations do not establish prospective patient recruitment or a clinical intervention.

Molecular cohorts support prognosis modeling with organoid and xenograft perturbation experiments. Laboratory interventions are not patient randomization; prospective patient accrual timing is not established.
Multi-omics characterization and enhancer experiments support a prognostic framework. Experimental molecular validation is not prospective clinical AI validation or a randomized patient intervention.
Transcriptomic and plasma datasets support diagnostic models, including an independent 540-person cohort. Independence alone does not establish prospective frozen-model testing or randomized care.
TCGA/CPTAC and multicenter data support immune-ratio models and survival associations. Registration and external prediction do not themselves establish prospective accrual or patient randomization.
Three-hospital imaging/report datasets support model and cost comparisons. The abstract does not establish prospective collection, frozen-model chronology, or actual randomized reporting workflows.

S-RACE curates hospital records for research and compares automated with manual curation. Infrastructure and model benchmarks do not establish randomized patient care or prospectively validated deployment.
